title: Honest ATT Interval Length When Shared Date Shocks Rarely Reveal Latent Confounders
banked_reason: tier=letter below novelty_target=field: even conditional on resolution, the proposed calibrated binary-sheet and known-channel frontier lacks a sufficiently literature-grounded consequence showing why this narrow experiment changes causal-inference practice or a broader established method class.

A field-tier novelty decision requires theorem-level comparison with weak/limited-overlap honest-inference work, including Rothe's robust ATE intervals and current weak-overlap DR inference, to exclude a transferable nonregular-inference result.
proof_attempt_summary: The run pivoted to sharp honest ATT interval length at the point-identified zero-excitation boundary and then revised the proposal to fully specify the estimator, interval, bounded fallback, and known finite-channel transfer. The revision cleared the sole well-posedness defect, but two independent review rounds still rated the contribution at letter tier because its consequence beyond the calibrated channel and its theorem-level weak-inference comparison were insufficient for the field floor. A field-tier successor would need a genuinely new estimated- or vanishing-channel frontier, not another presentation or literature-only revision of this result.
tldr: What honest ATT interval length is forced at an identified law when a shared date shock rarely reveals a latent confounder? Exact Bernoulli twins give a boundary lower bound of order \(N^{-1/2}+T^{-r}\), with \(r=\beta_e+\beta_m>q/2\). A fully specified split-sample signed estimator and binomially allocated interval are proposed to match it. The upper claim is a tentative theorem pending the fixed-degree signed variance and tail proof. A known finite-channel transfer class tests whether the mechanism extends beyond Gaussian measurements.
gap: The inspected proxy, HOIF, weak-factor, common-shock, and missing-panel results do not state an ATT interval-length theorem at a common-erasure point-identified boundary. The existence of an attaining signed interval under the full smoothness range remains unresolved.
fill: Establish the exact boundary lower obstruction, settle the matching signed-estimator upper question, and determine whether it transfers to known finite measurement channels with a fixed excited-state contrast.
